question.text: A series LCR circuit consists of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mo>Ω</mo></math>. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mo>Ω</mo></math>, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mo>Ω</mo></math>. The input voltage is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cos</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The amplitude of current, in the circuit, is _____  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Comparing input voltage with standard expression, V=V0cosωt, we get ω=100π.

Now, impedance Z=R2+XL-XC2

=802+100-402

=100Ω

Therefore, peak current

i0=V0Z=2500100 A=25 A
